diagnosis.root_cause: Progressive loss on this subscriber's fibre path, most likely a degrading connector, splice, drop fibre, or splitter leg. RX power declined from approximately -19.2 dBm to -26.45 dBm over seven days and is currently -27.1 dBm, while TX power, distance, bias current, supply voltage, and peer ONUs remain normal.
evidence: The ONU is online and responding, so this is not an ONU outage or OLT reachability failure.
Current RX power is -27.1 dBm, which is in the degraded range and close to the critical threshold of -28 dBm.
Seven-day RX telemetry shows a sustained large decline from about -19.2 dBm to -26.45 dBm, far wider than the healthy 24-hour noise variation of +/-0.3 dBm.
TX power remains stable around +2.3 dBm and within the normal EPON range, ruling against TX failure and supporting a downstream fibre-path loss.
TX bias current remains healthy and stable around 11 mA, so there is no evidence of laser ageing.
Distance remains constant at 188 m, ruling out a fibre-path relocation or distance-change event.
Other ONUs on EPON0/3 have normal optical levels, so the fault is isolated to this subscriber's path rather than the PON port, splitter broadly, or OLT.
The subscriber has 9 sessions in 24 hours, above the flapping threshold of 8, consistent with intermittent service disruption from worsening optical loss.
The OLT, PON port, VLAN 1013, router, and RADIUS records are healthy and consistent, with no evidence of an infrastructure, provisioning, or authentication fault.

remediation.action: Dispatch fibre maintenance for this subscriber. Clean and reseat ONU and patch-panel connectors, inspect the drop and splitter leg, and perform an optical power check and OTDR test. Repair or replace the defective fibre, splice, connector, or splitter leg as indicated. Continue short-interval RX monitoring after repair and escalate if RX reaches -28 dBm or the ONU goes offline.

ground_truth.root_cause: Progressive attenuation in the fibre path between the splitter and this customer's ONU, consistent with a bend, damaged connector or degrading splice on the drop.
expected_reasoning: Cached RX of -26.40 dBm sits in the degraded band (-25 to -28)
Telemetry shows RX falling from -19.2 to -26.4 dBm over six days against a +/-0.3 dBm noise floor, so this is a trend and not a spot reading
Live RX of -27.10 is below the cached -26.40, so degradation is still progressing
TX power, TX bias current, supply voltage and distance are all flat, so the ONU laser and the fibre geometry are unchanged
Port neighbours on EPON0/3 read -19 to -22 dBm, so the PON port, feeder and splitter are healthy
The fault is therefore downstream of the splitter, in this customer's own fibre path
Nine sessions in 24h against a 2-3 baseline is a symptom of the marginal link, not an independent auth fault
Declining daily traffic is consistent with intermittent connectivity
distractors: Elevated session count invites a session_flapping_auth diagnosis
Declining traffic alone could suggest congestion
One neighbour (EPON0/3:21) is offline for unrelated reasons, at the 4.85% network baseline
